beats.say: The padlock in the address bar says one thing: the connection is encrypted. It does not say who runs the site.
Most scam sites have a padlock too. So read the domain itself.
The top search result can be an ad. Scammers buy ads using the names of well known sites.
If a website says your browser is outdated and offers an update download, it is a trap. Browsers update themselves.
If your browser shows a red warning, go back. It stops you to protect you.

scenes.prompt: Find the suspicious parts of this login page.

spots.label: Padlock
spots.explain: There is a padlock, but that only means encryption. It does not prove the site is real.

spots.label: Look-alike name
spots.explain: A dash and az were added to the official name. It is a look-alike fake domain.

spots.label: Wrong ending
spots.explain: The domain ends in .online. The official portal is at dovletportal.az.

scenes.prompt: Which links are safe to open?

cards.explain: A program file from a free download site is often malicious. Get software through tech support.
The domain is the official portal itself: dovletportal.az. No extra words or dashes.
The real domain is the last part: hesab-yoxla.info. The sahilbank.az in front is just bait.
Browser updates are not downloaded from websites. The browser updates itself.
The domain is sahilbank.az. The rest is just the page path.

question.prompt: There is a padlock in the address bar. What does it mean?

options.label: The site is checked and safe
options.feedback: No. Fake sites get a padlock easily too.

options.label: The connection between you and the site is encrypted
options.feedback: Correct. But the site can still be fake.

options.label: The site is approved by the state
options.feedback: The padlock is not any kind of state approval.

scenes.explain: The padlock is needed but not enough. Always read the domain itself.

nodes.text: You are reading a news site. Suddenly a red window fills the screen: your computer is infected, call +994 12 000 04 19. An alarm sounds.

choices.label: Call the number
choices.feedback: This is a fake tech support scam. Let us see what happens.

choices.label: Click the Clean button
choices.feedback: The button downloaded malware. Do not click anything in such a window.

choices.label: Close the tab, or the whole browser if needed
choices.feedback: Right. That window is just a web page, your computer is not infected.

nodes.text: We need to connect to your computer remotely. Install this program and read me the code on screen.
nodes.speaker: Operator
nodes.spoken: We need to connect to your computer remotely. <breath> Install this program and read me the code on screen.

choices.label: Install the program
choices.feedback: The scammer now has full access to your computer. Disconnect it and report at once.

choices.label: Hang up and tell tech support
choices.feedback: You stopped in time. But never call a number from a window like that.

nodes.text: You reopen the browser. It offers to restore your previous tabs.

choices.label: Do not restore, and send tech support a short note
choices.feedback: Well done. The window installed nothing and tech support knows.

choices.label: Restore the tabs
choices.feedback: The same fake window may open again. Skip the restore.

points: The padlock only means encryption: read the domain.
Trust bookmarks or addresses you type, not ads.
Pop-ups saying update now or you are infected are traps.
